name: MedTech Solutions: 3-year TCO, stay vs migrate
assumptions: data_tb, data_growth
200 TB growing 20-25%/yr (coursework: MedTech current state); 22% used
hardware_refresh_capex
12 virtualization hosts + SAN controllers + switches due for refresh (aging infrastructure), ~$600k over a 5-year life
storage_cost_per_tb
Enterprise SAN, ~$1,200 per usable TB over 5 years
facilities_per_year
Two data centers: space, power, cooling, physical security
licenses_per_year
Virtualization, backup, OS and monitoring licenses (virtualization pricing rose sharply after 2024)
ops_fte 6 -> 4.5
Infrastructure staff; cloud removes hardware/facility work but adds platform, FinOps and security work - a 25% reduction, not 50%
instances 96
120 VMs minus retired tools (10% of apps) and the billing system moved to SaaS (Repurchase)
avg_instance_monthly $140
Blended on-demand price after rightsizing (mix of 2-4 vCPU instances, some Windows)
savings_plan 30% at 30/70/80% coverage
1-year Compute Savings Plans bought only once usage is measured (coursework: 'no commitment until baseline known')
storage tiers
Imaging archive is 60% of data and needs millisecond access, so Glacier Instant Retrieval rather than Deep Archive
egress 10 TB/month
Telehealth, image viewing by referring clinics, partner feeds
security_ops 10%, support 7%
GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, CloudTrail, CloudWatch; Business support tier
migration_one_time $450k
Partner assistance, training (coursework resource plan), migration tooling, extra testing
dual_running 70% / 20% / 0%
Data centers can't be switched off until the last wave (18-month roadmap); staff counted once

sensitivity.label: Cloud ops staff stays at 6 FTE vs drops to 4
No Savings Plans vs aggressive coverage (50/90/90%)
Slow exit (90/40/10% dual running) vs fast (50/10/0%)
